status_summary: The House Appropriations Committee's fiscal year 2026 Commerce, Justice, Science bill summary, updated 2025-07-23, listed directing the re-establishment of the DOJ China Initiative, and the accompanying committee report directed the National Security Division to re-establish an office to counter PRC espionage and influence efforts. Press reports in January 2026 said the language was removed before final passage, and the act was enacted as Public Law 119-74 on 2026-01-23. No Justice Department announcement or directive restarting the initiative was found.

timeline.event: The House Appropriations Committee's summary of its fiscal year 2026 Commerce, Justice, Science bill listed directing the re-establishment of the DOJ China Initiative.

The Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 was enacted as Public Law 119-74; press reports said the China Initiative language had been removed before final passage.

title: Restart the DOJ China Initiative
uncertainties: The committee report and the final explanatory statement were not opened; the report directive is described in a letter from members opposing it, and its removal rests on two secondary sources, one from an advocacy group. The visible part of the enacted text shows only National Security Division funding. The 2025-02-05 closure of the Foreign Influence Task Force concerns foreign-influence work and is not a restart of the initiative. A systematic search of Justice Department releases was not done.
